title: Triplets That Sum to Zero

concept.title: Fix one number, then two pointers
body: To find three numbers with sum 0, **sort** the array, fix the first number `a[i]`, and look for a pair in the rest that adds up to `-a[i]` with two pointers, as in a sorted pair-sum search. That is O(n) per fixed number, O(n^2) in total.

body.code:
a.sort()
for i in range(n - 2):
    if i > 0 and a[i] == a[i - 1]: continue     # same first number as before
    l, r = i + 1, n - 1
    while l < r:
        t = a[i] + a[l] + a[r]
        if t < 0: l += 1
        elif t > 0: r -= 1
        else:
            count += 1; l += 1; r -= 1
            while l < r and a[l] == a[l - 1]: l += 1

body: Duplicates are skipped at every level (the first number, and the second number after a hit), so that each different triplet of values is counted once.

statement: Given `n` integers, count the different triplets of **values** `(x, y, z)` with `x <= y <= z` and `x + y + z = 0`. Two triplets are the same if they contain the same values. Elements at different positions may be used together, but each position only once in a triplet.
outputFormat: Print the number of different triplets.
hints: Fix the smallest number a[i], then look for a pair with sum -a[i] using two pointers.
Skip equal values for the fixed number and, after finding a triplet, for the left pointer.

solution.complexity: Time O(n^2), space O(1) besides sorting.
